query: The Tipping Tray {A first-year is coming down the aisle with a tray of eight soup bowls stacked like a tower, and a bench leg is sticking out right where they'll step.|The same first-year, a bigger tray, a different bench leg. Some people never learn; some benches don't either.|The tray, the first-year, the bench. You can almost hear the crash before it happens.} Lunge for the tray {You catch the tray an inch from disaster with soup up to your wrists. The first-year looks at you as if you'd stopped the sun.|You get a hand under it and one bowl of eight goes over. The first-year counts it as a miracle.|Tray, bowls, first-year, all upright, and not a drop on your sleeve. The table nearest applauds with spoons.} {You get there just in time to wear the soup. All eight bowls. It's leek.|You catch the first-year and miss the tray. The crash is heard in the kitchens; the cook comes out to see.|You lunge, the bench catches you too, and you both go down in a lake of soup.} Move your own bowl out of range {You lift your bowl to safety and watch it happen. The leg, the trip, the crash. Nobody blames you. You blame you, a little.|You move your bowl. The first-year doesn't move theirs. Somebody else catches the tray, and the first-year thanks them with shining eyes.|Out of range, and dry. The crash is spectacular. You help pick up the bowls afterwards, which is something.} Kick the bench leg in first {You see it a heartbeat early, the leg and the step and the tray, and nudge the bench in with your heel. The first-year sails past and never knows.|A glimpse ahead and a small shove. The tray arrives whole. The first-year doesn't notice; you do, and it's lovely.|You move the bench before the first-year has even turned into the aisle. The cook, watching from the hatch, raises her ladle at you like a salute.}
